chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said:
I asked him about the instigation (fighting) between animals, so he said: 'All of it is abhorred, except for the dog.'

key_terms.التَّحْرِيشِ: Instigation or incitement, specifically referring to making animals fight each other
key_terms.الْبَهَائِمِ: Animals (specifically beasts of burden or livestock in this context)
key_terms.مَكْرُوهٌ: Abhorred or disliked (a category of legal ruling in Shia fiqh)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on instigating animals to fight?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the general prohibition of 'al-tahris' (instigating animals to fight) as makruh, with a specific exception for dogs, reflecting the practical utility of canine combat in hunting and warfare. Scholars note that this ruling distinguishes dogs from other livestock, acknowledging their unique role in traditional Arab society while maintaining the principle of avoiding unnecessary harm or frivolity in animal treatment.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Al Abbas, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the instigation between the animals, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘All of it is abhorred, except for the dog’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from abu al-‘Abbas who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about instigating animals against each other.
He (the Imam) said, ‘All of it is detestable except dogs.’”
